question: In a circle, chord AB subtends an angle of 60° at the center. What is the angle subtended by the same chord AB at any point C on the major arc (opposite side of the center)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The angle subtended by a chord at the center is always double the angle subtended by it at any point on the remaining part of the circle (major arc).

⇒ Angle at major arc = (Angle at center) ÷ 2

⇒ Angle = 60° ÷ 2 = 30°

**∴ The correct answer is 30°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Angle subtended by chord AB at the center O, ∠AOB = 60°

Point C is any point on the major arc of the circle.

**Formula Used:**

According to the circle theorem, the angle subtended by an arc at the center is double the angle subtended by it at any remaining part of the circle.

⇒ ∠AOB = 2 × ∠ACB

**Calculations:**

⇒ 60° = 2 × ∠ACB

⇒ ∠ACB = 60° ÷ 2

⇒ ∠ACB = 30°

**∴ The correct answer is 30°.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Angles in the Same Segment

Angles subtended by the same arc at any point on the remaining part of the circle are always equal.

Cyclic Quadrilateral

If a quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle, the sum of its opposite interior angles is always 180°.

Angle in a Semicircle

The angle subtended by the diameter at any point on the circumference of the circle is always a right angle (90°).
